answer: At dawn, each bidding agent must anchor one merchant-signed receipt — a coffee, a bus ticket, a ferrous bolt — hashed on-ledger. First, the agent buys something real for at least $3 and gets the receipt signed. Second, the registry verifies the signature and checks the hash was never used. Third, receipts die after one epoch, so last week's coffee cannot bid today. A 1,000-clone farm needs 1,000 genuine purchases per epoch — $3,000 a day — while one honest agent spends $3 on breakfast. Like a nadir tide stranding every beached boat, the rule leaves clones nowhere to hide.
